claim: Nodal signals pattern the germ layers during vertebrate embryogenesis.
source: During vertebrate embryogenesis, the germ layers are patterned by secreted Nodal signals.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a foundational statement about Nodal function.

claim: In the classical model, Nodals elicit signaling by binding to a complex comprising Type I/II Activin receptors (Acvr) and the co-receptor Tdgf1.
source: In the classical model, Nodals elicit signaling by binding to a complex comprising Type I/II Activin receptors (Acvr) and the co-receptor Tdgf1.
evidence: This is a statement about the classical model of Nodal signaling, supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: It is currently unclear whether receptor binding can affect the distribution of Nodals themselves through the embryo.
source: However, it is currently unclear whether receptor binding can also affect the distribution of Nodals themselves through the embryo
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge, indicating a gap in understanding.

claim: It is unknown which of the putative Acvr paralogs mediate Nodal signaling in zebrafish.
source: it is unknown which of the putative Acvr paralogs mediate Nodal signaling in zebrafish.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge, indicating a gap in understanding.

claim: Three Type I (Acvr1) and four Type II (Acvr2) homologs were characterized in zebrafish.
source: Here, we characterize three Type I (Acvr1) and four Type II (Acvr2) homologs
evidence: This is a statement about the research conducted in this study.

claim: Except for Acvr1c, all receptor-encoding transcripts are maternally deposited and present during zebrafish embryogenesis.
source: show that – except for Acvr1c – all receptor-encoding transcripts are maternally deposited and present during zebrafish embryogenesis.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on expression analysis.

claim: The Acvr2 homologs function partly redundantly and partially independently of Nodal to pattern the early zebrafish embryo.
source: We discovered that the Acvr2 homologs function partly redundantly and partially independently of Nodal to pattern the early zebrafish embryo
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on loss-of-function experiments.

claim: The Type I receptors Acvr1b-a and Acvr1b-b redundantly act as major mediators of Nodal signaling.
source: whereas the Type I receptors Acvr1b-a and Acvr1b-b redundantly act as major mediators of Nodal signaling.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on loss-of-function experiments.

claim: Feedback-regulated Type I receptors and co-receptors can directly influence the diffusion and distribution of Nodals.
source: By combining quantitative analyses with expression manipulations, we found that feedback-regulated Type I receptors and co-receptors can directly influence the diffusion and distribution of Nodals
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on quantitative imaging and expression manipulation experiments.

claim: Feedback-regulated Type I receptors and co-receptors provide a mechanism for the spatial restriction of Nodal signaling during germ layer patterning.
source: providing a mechanism for the spatial restriction of Nodal signaling during germ layer patterning.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings, suggesting a mechanism based on the data.

claim: Nodal is one of the key regulators of vertebrate development and is required to specify mesoderm and endoderm during germ layer formation.
source: The TGF-β superfamily member Nodal is one of the key regulators of vertebrate development and is required to specify mesoderm and endoderm (collectively termed mesendoderm) during germ layer formation (Schier, 2009).
evidence: This is a statement about Nodal function supported by a citation.

claim: Nodal ligands signal through a receptor complex comprising Type I and Type II single-transmembrane serine/threonine kinase receptors.
source: In the classical model, Nodal ligands signal through a receptor complex comprising Type I and Type II single-transmembrane serine/threonine kinase receptors (Attisano and Wrana, 2002; Shi and Massagué, 2003; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a statement about the classical model of Nodal signaling, supported by citations and a figure.

claim: Nodal signaling requires the presence of an EGF-CFC co-receptor to activate signaling.
source: Unlike other members of the TGF-β superfamily, Nodal signaling additionally requires the presence of an EGF-CFC co-receptor to activate signaling.
evidence: This is a statement about a unique requirement of Nodal signaling.

claim: Nodal directly binds to Type II receptors and the EGF-CFC co-receptor Tdgf1, which in turn mediates the recruitment of the Type I receptors.
source: Our current understanding of Nodal signaling is that Nodal directly binds to Type II receptors and the EGF-CFC co-receptor Tdgf1, which in turn mediates the recruitment of the Type I receptors.
evidence: This is a statement about the current understanding of Nodal signaling mechanism.

claim: Upon oligomerization of the receptor complex, Type II receptors phosphorylate the Type I receptors in their GS domains.
source: Upon oligomerization of the receptor complex, Type II receptors phosphorylate the Type I receptors in their GS domains
evidence: This is a statement about the mechanism of Nodal signaling.

claim: Type I receptors recruit and phosphorylate the C-terminal SSXS motif of the receptor-regulated Smad (R-Smad) proteins Smad2 and Smad3.
source: leading to the recruitment and phosphorylation of the C-terminal SSXS motif of the receptor-regulated Smad (R-Smad) proteins Smad2 and Smad3 by the Type I receptor.
evidence: This is a statement about the mechanism of Nodal signaling, supported by citations.

claim: The activated pSmad2/pSmad3 proteins associate with the co-factor Smad4 and translocate into the nucleus, where they activate target gene expression.
source: The activated pSmad2/pSmad3 proteins associate with the co-factor Smad4 and translocate into the nucleus, where they activate target gene expression (Hill, 2018; Macías-Silva et al., 1996; Shi and Massagué, 2003; Yeo and Whitman, 2001; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a statement about the mechanism of Nodal signaling, supported by citations and a figure.

claim: In zebrafish, mesendoderm patterning depends on the two secreted Nodal signals Squint (Sqt) and Cyclops (Cyc).
source: In zebrafish, mesendoderm patterning depends on the two secreted Nodal signals Squint (Sqt) and Cyclops (Cyc) (Dougan et al., 2003; Rogers and Müller, 2019; Schier, 2009; Shen, 2007).
evidence: This is a statement about Nodal signaling in zebrafish, supported by citations.

claim: Nodal expression begins in the yolk syncytial layer at the embryonic margin during the blastula stage and then spreads into the embryo, generating a Nodal signaling gradient.
source: Nodal expression begins in the yolk syncytial layer at the embryonic margin during the blastula stage and then spreads into the embryo, generating a Nodal signaling gradient.
evidence: This is a statement about the spatiotemporal dynamics of Nodal expression in zebrafish.

claim: The Nodal signaling gradient is translated into different mesendodermal cell fates depending on the signaling level and target gene induction kinetics.
source: This gradient is translated into different mesendodermal cell fates depending on the signaling level and target gene induction kinetics (Dubrulle et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about how Nodal signaling patterns cell fates, supported by a citation.

claim: Loss of Nodal signaling causes absence of endoderm as well as trunk and head mesoderm, which leads to cyclopia due to a failure to separate the eye fields, resulting in embryonic lethality.
source: Loss of Nodal signaling causes absence of endoderm as well as trunk and head mesoderm, which leads to cyclopia due to a failure to separate the eye fields, resulting in embryonic lethality (Dubrulle et al., 2015; Feldman et al., 1998; Gritsman et al., 1999).
evidence: This is a statement about the phenotype of Nodal loss-of-function, supported by citations.

claim: Nodal signaling is antagonized by the secreted long-range feedback inhibitor Lefty, which is also produced at the margin.
source: Nodal signaling is antagonized by the secreted long-range feedback inhibitor Lefty, which is also produced at the margin (Meno et al., 1999; Thisse and Thisse, 1999).
evidence: This is a statement about Nodal signaling regulation, supported by citations.

claim: Establishment and maintenance of a correct signaling range is crucial for correct development.
source: Establishment and maintenance of a correct signaling range is crucial for correct development
evidence: This is a general statement about the importance of signaling range.

claim: Excess Nodal signaling, for example in lefty mutants, can cause severe patterning defects and embryonic lethality.
source: as also excess Nodal signaling – for example in lefty mutants – can cause severe patterning defects and embryonic lethality (Almuedo-Castillo et al., 2018; Rogers et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about the consequences of excess Nodal signaling, supported by citations.

claim: Squint and Cyclops proteins have a lower effective diffusivity than their inhibitors Lefty1 (Lft1) and Lefty2 (Lft2).
source: Measurements of active GFP-tagged fusions showed that Squint and Cyclops proteins have a lower effective diffusivity than their inhibitors Lefty1 (Lft1) and Lefty2 (Lft2) (Müller et al., 2012; Rogers and Müller, 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about the biophysical properties of Nodal and Lefty proteins, supported by citations.

claim: The mobility difference between Nodal and Lefty is proposed to be due to interactions between Nodal ligands and membrane-bound diffusion regulators, whereas Lefty proteins move more freely in the extracellular space.
source: It has been proposed that this mobility difference is due to interactions between Nodal ligands and membrane-bound diffusion regulators, whereas Lefty proteins move more freely in the extracellular space (Müller et al., 2012; Müller et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism for the mobility difference, supported by citations.

claim: Nodal's signaling range and distribution dramatically increase in the absence of the zebrafish Tdgf1 co-receptor homolog Oep.
source: Indeed, Nodal's signaling range and distribution dramatically increase in the absence of the zebrafish Tdgf1 co-receptor homolog Oep (Lord et al., 2021)
evidence: This is a statement about the effect of Oep on Nodal distribution, supported by a citation.

claim: Single-molecule imaging has shown that the fraction of molecules in the bound state is larger for Nodal than for Lefty.
source: and single-molecule imaging has recently shown that the fraction of molecules in the bound state is larger for Nodal than for Lefty (Kuhn et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a statement about the binding behavior of Nodal and Lefty, supported by a citation.

claim: Nodals strongly bind to the zebrafish Type II receptor Acvr2b-a in vivo.
source: Since Nodals strongly bind to the zebrafish Type II receptor Acvr2b-a in vivo (Wang et al., 2016)
evidence: This is a statement about the interaction between Nodal and Acvr2b-a, supported by a citation.

claim: The main Nodal receptors might act as diffusion regulators.
source: the main Nodal receptors themselves might also act as diffusion regulators.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the strong binding of Nodal to Acvr2b-a.

claim: It is unclear whether the strong ligand-receptor interaction influences Nodal dispersal.
source: However, it is unclear whether this strong ligand-receptor interaction indeed influences Nodal dispersal
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge, indicating a gap in understanding.

claim: It is unclear whether receptor binding affects Nodal diffusion or stability in the embryo.
source: whether receptor binding affects Nodal diffusion or stability in the embryo
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge, indicating a gap in understanding.

claim: It is unclear what role other putative Type I and Type II Acvr receptors play in the propagation of Nodal signaling through the embryo.
source: and what role other putative Type I and Type II Acvr receptors play in the propagation of Nodal signaling through the embryo.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge, indicating a gap in understanding.

claim: The two mouse, frog and human Type I receptors Acvr1b and Acvr1c and the two Type II receptors Acvr2a and Acvr2b were identified using in vitro binding and target induction assays.
source: The two mouse, frog and human Type I receptors Acvr1b (also known as Alk4/TARAM-A) and Acvr1c (also known as Alk7) and the two Type II receptors Acvr2a and Acvr2b were identified using in vitro binding and target induction assays
evidence: This is a statement about how these receptors were identified, supported by citations.

claim: Mutations in Acvr1b, Acvr1c, Acvr2a, and Acvr2b cause developmental defects in mouse, frog, and human.
source: and cause developmental defects when mutated (Gritsman et al., 1999; Gu et al., 1998; Kosaki et al., 1999; Matzuk et al., 1995; Oh and Li, 1997; Reissmann et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a statement about the phenotypes of receptor mutants, supported by citations.

claim: Except for the zebrafish co-receptor Oep, no zebrafish Nodal receptor mutants are known to recapitulate Nodal loss-of-function phenotypes.
source: Surprisingly, except for the zebrafish co-receptor Oep (Gritsman et al., 1999), no zebrafish Nodal receptor mutants are known to recapitulate Nodal loss-of-function phenotypes
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge regarding zebrafish Nodal receptor mutants.

claim: It is unknown which of the receptor paralogs mediate endogenous Nodal signaling during germ layer formation in zebrafish.
source: and although zebrafish are widely used to investigate Nodal signaling during development, it is unknown which of the receptor paralogs mediate endogenous Nodal signaling during germ layer formation.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge, indicating a gap in understanding.

claim: Several loss-of-function mutants were generated to assess compound loss-of-function phenotypes.
source: To understand the role of the zebrafish receptor homologs in Nodal distribution and signaling, we generated several loss-of-function mutants and used them together with combinatorial morpholino knockdown and CRISPR F0 knockout (KO) approaches to assess compound loss-of-function phenotypes.

claim: Loss of individual receptor function did not cause obvious patterning defects.
source: Strikingly, loss of individual receptor function did not cause obvious patterning defects.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on loss-of-function experiments.

claim: Severe patterning phenotypes and embryonic lethality were observed with combinatorial loss of putative Type II Acvr receptors.
source: Severe patterning phenotypes and embryonic lethality were observed with combinatorial loss of putative Type II Acvr receptors
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on loss-of-function experiments.

claim: The defects caused by combinatorial loss of Type II Acvr receptors were at least partly independent of Nodal signaling.
source: but the defects were at least partly independently of Nodal signaling.

claim: The combined loss of the Type I receptors acvr1b-a and acvr1b-b phenocopied known Nodal loss-of-function phenotypes.
source: Instead, only the combined loss of the Type I receptors acvr1b-a and acvr1b-b phenocopied known Nodal loss-of-function phenotypes (Dubrulle et al., 2015; Feldman et al., 1998; Gritsman et al., 1999)
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on loss-of-function experiments, supported by citations.

claim: Acvr1b-a and acvr1b-b are the main Type I receptors that mediate early Nodal signaling in zebrafish.
source: identifying these receptors as the main Type I receptors that mediate early Nodal signaling in zebrafish.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study based on loss-of-function experiments.

claim: Type I receptor and co-receptor levels can modulate Nodal mobility.
source: Using quantitative imaging assays, we found that Type I receptor and co-receptor levels can modulate Nodal mobility

claim: Type I receptor and co-receptor levels directly influence the distribution of Nodal in the embryo.
source: and thereby directly influence the distribution of Nodal in the embryo

claim: Type I receptor and co-receptor levels provide a mechanism for the spatial restriction of Nodal signaling during germ layer patterning.
source: providing a mechanism for the spatial restriction of Nodal signaling during germ layer patterning.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings, suggesting a mechanism based on the data.

claim: Zebrafish have three putative Type I receptors: Acvr1b-a, Acvr1b-b, and Acvr1c.
source: our analysis yielded further potential Nodal receptor paralogous sequences named Acvr1b-b, Acvr2a-b and Acvr2b-b (Funkenstein et al., 2012; Li et al., 2019), respectively, resulting in a total of three putative Type I and four putative Type II receptors.

claim: Zebrafish have four putative Type II receptors: Acvr2a-a, Acvr2a-b, Acvr2b-a, and Acvr2b-b.
source: our analysis yielded further potential Nodal receptor paralogous sequences named Acvr1b-b, Acvr2a-b and Acvr2b-b (Funkenstein et al., 2012; Li et al., 2019), respectively, resulting in a total of three putative Type I and four putative Type II receptors.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on homology searches.

claim: The start of the acvr2a-b gene's coding sequence and the full amino acid sequence of the receptor was not resolved, and corresponding predictions differed between genome assemblies.
source: For Acvr2a-b, the start of the gene's coding sequence and the full amino acid sequence of the receptor was not resolved, and corresponding predictions differed between genome assemblies.

claim: 5'RACE was performed to map the start of acvr2a-b to chrUn_KN150226v1.

claim: Reconstruction of a putative phylogenetic tree shows a close clustering of the zebrafish receptors with their human and mouse paralogs.
source: Reconstruction of a putative phylogenetic tree shows a close clustering of the zebrafish receptors with their human and mouse paralogs
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on phylogenetic analysis.

claim: The highest sequence similarity was found between the zebrafish Type I receptors Acvr1b-a and Acvr1b-b.
source: and the highest sequence similarity was found between the zebrafish Type I receptors Acvr1b-a and Acvr1b-b (Figure 1B).

claim: All putative homologs have the typical features of Type I and Type II receptors, including a signal peptide, TGF-β receptor domain, transmembrane domain, cytosolic kinase domain and a GS domain in case of the Type I receptors.
source: All putative homologs have the typical features of Type I and Type II receptors, including a signal peptide, TGF-β receptor domain, transmembrane domain, cytosolic kinase domain and a GS domain in case of the Type I receptors (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B-H).

claim: The transcripts of most receptor paralogs are present at early blastula and gastrula stages and before the maternal-zygotic transition, suggesting that they are maternally deposited.

claim: Expression of the identified receptors persists throughout larval development up to 4 days post-fertilization (dpf).
source: Expression of the identified receptors persists throughout larval development up to 4 days post-fertilization (dpf).

source: The only receptor-encoding gene that does not seem to be expressed during early development is the Type I receptor homolog acvr1c, which is first detected at 4 dpf (Figure 1C).

claim: All putative receptors except for acvr1c are expressed at the developmental stages during which Nodal signaling patterns the germ layers.
source: Therefore, all putative receptors except for acvr1c are expressed at the developmental stages, during which Nodal signaling patterns the germ layers.

claim: Transcripts of all putative Nodal Type I and II receptors – with the exception of acvr1c – are evenly distributed at the two-cell stage, consistent with maternal deposition.

claim: During early gastrulation (shield stage), most receptors are ubiquitously expressed throughout the embryo.
source: During early gastrulation (shield stage), most receptors are ubiquitously expressed throughout the embryo (Garg et al., 1999; Nagaso et al., 1999)

claim: acvr1c is not expressed during early gastrulation (shield stage).

claim: acvr2a-aSA34654 and acvr2a-bSA18285 mutants were obtained from the European Zebrafish Resource Center (EZRC).

source: This is in stark contrast to the mouse Type IIB receptor mutants that exhibit severe malformations during early embryonic development (Gu et al., 1998; Oh and Li, 1997).
